## v1.2.13 (planned, 2026-10-11)

Contraction: fewer lines, no behaviour change, with v1.2.12's tests and checked models as the net under it. Passes in this order, one writer per package: remove dead and stale code; adopt the Go standard library or established packages where they replace hand-rolled code; run go fix (and gopls modernize) over all Go code; pull code the tools share into modules, then code the modules share into modules; make each test minimal, on test frameworks and shared helper modules. The module pass also covers the copies across the two repositories: 59 same-named packages exist as separate copies in nova-sprint and nova-tools (about 71,500 shared lines, measured 2026-10-11 at nova-sprint 15c779c and nova-tools 2a648d8). Each gets one owner, nova-sprint as with nova-roadmap, and the other repository imports it: the identical copies first, then the diverged ones (member, fleet, cardtree, tool, and parts of friend and swarm), reconciled under v1.2.12's tests. The first named entries are the nova-roadmap extraction and the brief boilerplate moving into the card contract. Measured as lines per repository and package, product against test, from a baseline taken before the first pass.

- **Extract the roadmap tool into nova-roadmap** (planned). The roadmap and fixes code exists twice: here as internal/roadmap, internal/roadmapdoc, tools/roadmap and the nova-work roadmap verbs (about 3,100 lines with their tests), and in nova-tools as internal/roadmap, internal/roadmap/sexp and tools/roadmap (about 1,300 lines with their tests, about 930 without), with two diverging copies of the generator. Unify the s-expression format first; then one module and one CLI, nova-roadmap, living in this repository (a module and cmd/nova-roadmap): it reads and writes the data, renders ROADMAP.md and FIXES.md, and runs the sync check. Both repositories use it and delete their own copies: this one its internal copies, nova-tools by importing nova-roadmap from this repository. Net fewer lines. Its s-expressions stay importable later as a node by nova-work; that import is a v1.3 item, not this one. From: the owner, 2026-10-11: v1.2.13 contraction, pass 4 (shared code into modules); nova-roadmap lives in nova-sprint.
- **Brief boilerplate moves into the card contract** (planned). A brief names the card contract instead of carrying its text, so briefs are shorter and the contract has one copy. The RULES, LEDGERS, WALL AND TOOLS and BUDGET blocks, about 6 KB of every 10 to 11 KB brief, are referenced once from the card contract instead of repeated in each brief, and a card lint refuses repeated instruction text in a brief. Agreed with the owner on 2026-10-11 as a lesson from the Cockroach Labs write-up "Five months treating bugs like patients" (MOLT Sinai). From: roadmap item briefs-by-reference.

## v1.2.14 (planned, 2026-10-11)

The next small fixes, one concern each, including the defects v1.2.12's tests find, a circuit breaker on the review loop, and a red base pushed to the coordinator.

- **What an operator reads matches the bare-merge refusal and the key rest** (planned). A late-merge judgment prints land for a real store and the bare merge only as the twin's form; the CLI, first-lap and test docs mark the bare merge twin-only (play is a twin tool); the spec and comments say a key rest ends only by routes wake, never by funded or a payment, and a test shows a balance poll cannot end one. From: readers' notes on nova-sprint PR #49 and PR #50.
- **A hook stays live while its re-challenge is in bound** (planned). The record's Live was the proof's bound alone, so a seat answering in time was refused HookFirst between the proof's Live and a re-challenge's own bound whenever a slow look sent the challenge late. The server now moves Live to the re-challenge's own bound through the record's one writer; a write that fails keeps the earlier bound (the safe side) and says so on the server's line. Test: TestARechallengeKeepsTheHookLiveUntilItsOwnBound. From: v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11, section 9 row D6; code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba.
- **brief check runs every add check without a write** (planned). An add's refusals arrived one class at a time, so a brief writer learned of the next only after fixing the last. The new read-only verb brief check runs every check add runs, in add's order, over every brief, and collects every finding: the id, the size bound, shared PATHS, the card lint, the WHO, base, TLA+ records, card checks, brief-base, paths-admit and sprint-base holds, then the add step's own plan on one read-only snapshot. It prints one CHECK line a finding and a BRIEF CHECK files=<n> findings=<m> line, --json prints the findings as one array, exits 0 with no finding, 1 with any, 2 for usage or an unreadable file, and 3 when the store does not answer and the store-free checks found nothing. Nothing is written and the brief decision is never asked. Tests: the twin store names two findings of three briefs in one call and leaves its keys equal, the clean brief is exit 0, and a brief over the size bound and a lint finding in one file are both said. From: tmp/next-sprint-cards/TOOLING-FROM-THE-SEAT-2026-10-11.md item 2; the owner, 2026-10-11.
- **add --partial holds back what fails and admits the rest** (planned). add was all or none: one failing brief refused the whole call, so the coordinator looped add, read the refusals, moved the refused files aside and added again. add --partial, with --brief-dir or a repeated --brief-file only, runs brief check's collector over every brief, holds back every brief with a finding and every card that needs a held card through its Needs: or DEPENDS-ON: line or --needs, transitively, then runs the add step's own plan over the rest and holds back each card its Refused list names with the cards that need it, planning the write again without them; the rounds are bounded by the number of cards, and nothing is written for a held card. The rest are admitted in one store write, the brief decision asked for them only. It prints one HELD <id>: <its first finding or refusal> or HELD <id>: needs <other>, held back line per held card, then the add's closing line, and exits 0 when every card was admitted, 1 when some were held and the rest written, and 2 when none could be admitted or for usage. --partial is refused with ids, --count, --sentinel or --land-protected, since a marked first add is one step. Without --partial add is all or none as before. Tests: five briefs, b2 with a PRIORITY add refuses and b4 DEPENDS-ON b2, admit b1, b3 and b5, hold b2 and b4 with their two lines, exit 1, and leave exactly three new cards; a brief the plan refuses at the write is held with its refusal and the others land; with every brief clean the exit is 0, as add without the flag. From: this card; tmp/next-sprint-cards/TOOLING-FROM-THE-SEAT-2026-10-11.md item 1 (the owner, 2026-10-11: "Whatever you are doing manually now, consider adding tool support for it to nova sprint.").
- **The seat's push loop goes on at the epoch a clear leaves it** (planned). inbox --wait and --push re-read the sprint's active epoch when a clear advances it under the loop: the look at the inbox is never refused MEMBEREPOCH by the epoch the clear left, the wait ends at the clear as at a machine stop, the inbox reporting the clear's happened line, and the seat's push loop keeps running, pushing the new epoch's judgments. A step in flight still holds its epoch: a tick at a clear stops there. From: the seat ledger v1.2.4-held-2026-10-10.md, bug 6.
- **add can mark a new stream for protected branches** (planned). add --land-protected marks a new stream atomically with its first card, so a point-release stream can admit a card based on main or dev without a sentinel card or a follow-up stream set. From: the seat ledger bug 14.
- **An idle episode that ends with no width or no work says why, never working again** (planned). TickIdle ends an idle episode for four reasons and only one is a recovery. The fleet working at half its width again (a) keeps NIdleCleared, "working again"; no card waits (b), no width up -- every member down, held or drained (c) -- and the fleet's work switched off (d) push a new happened type NIdleEnded, "the fleet's idle episode ended", naming the cause: "no card waits", "no width up: every member is down, held or drained (fleet up <member> --width <n>)", or "the fleet's work is switched off (set --fleet on)". Both properties are cleared on every end as before. docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md section 14 says which end says what. The episode machine is unchanged (AlarmOncePerEpisode, ClearFollowsAlarm), so tla/SprintRules.tla, Part "idle", is not edited. TestAnIdleEpisodeEndedByNoWidthNeverSaysWorkingAgain (red on the base), TestAnIdleEpisodeEndedByWorkSaysWorkingAgain, TestAnIdleEpisodeEndedByNoWaitingCardSaysTheCause, TestAnIdleEpisodeEndedByTheFleetSwitchSaysTheCause. From: the seat's v1.2.14 audit, 2026-10-11 (TickIdle says "working again" when width is 0), checked against nova-sprint main 00c54ba; this card.
- **The tick judges and pushes a landing stall, and pushes every landing** (planned). When cards wait in review or merging and no card has landed for one minute of running time (the landing_stall_bound setting, default LandingStallBound; the owner's number: "10 minute stall watch is too long. 1 minute."), the tick end raises one judgment NLandingStall, "landing stalled", to the coordinator with its cause breakdown: the reads out (count, by reader, oldest age), the cards waiting on the coordinator's judgment (count, oldest alias; a review where every card waits on the coordinator is named the seat's stall), the accepted and not merged (count, the stream's merge state), the lander's last refusal (card and reason) and the base's red CI. The alarm runs in the deadlines part (TickDeadlines), independent of the idle alarm, and the merge step writes the facts it measures from, on the work table: last_landing (the stamp of the last card that landed) and land_refusal (the lander's last refusal). The episode lives on the work table's properties (landing_stall_since, landing_stall_said), is re-raised each bound it holds (the open judgment rewritten in place with fresh facts) and clears on the next landing with the happened NLandingAgain, "landing again after <d>"; a sprint with nothing in review or merging raises none. docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md, the judgments section, names the stall, its bound, its breakdown and its clear. Every landing is pushed to the coordinator as it happens (landingPush): one happened NLanding, "landed <card>" a line, with the card's stream, head, the one-line :title and :text of its ledger entry (read from the work card), and the attempts and reads it took; a batch in one tick is one push with a line a card. The model card tla-sprintrules-landing-stall-liveness is its own card. Tests TestLandingStallIsJudgedWhenCardsWaitAndNothingLands, TestLandingStallIsReRaisedEachBound, TestLandingStallClearsOnTheNextLanding, TestNoStallWithNothingWaiting, TestAStallOfCardsOnTheCoordinatorIsNamedTheSeatsStall, TestEveryLandingIsPushedToTheCoordinator, TestMergeWritesTheLandingStallFacts, TestMergeWritesTheLandersLastRefusal, TestTickDeadlinesRaisesTheLandingStall. From: the owner, 2026-10-11 ~12:20-12:45 PM ET, after landed sat at 68/294 +0/30m for half an hour while 76 cards sat in review and 68 in fix and no judgment reached the seat: "I shouldn't need to tell you this, you should just get a push notification about it" and "Fix the fucking gaps in push notifications"; this card.
- **backup --out passes on a fleet that is beating** (planned). The restore check sets aside what a live member's beat rewrites while the dump is taken (the fleet table's revision, a fleet row's place, load text and up or down status) and compares everything else exactly, so a running fleet no longer fails the check; a held status, a missing row or a changed card still does. From: pre-clear backup, 2026-10-10 (8 fleet parts differed).
- **Card lint refuses valid cards: make gates and text inside fenced blocks** (planned). Card lint rejects make-driven gates and flags parent paths or absolute paths quoted inside fenced blocks. It should accept both. From: issue #1994; issue #2302; issue #3470.
- **One column field every reader agrees on** (planned). Card output carries a single column field so a card's state is not confused with the state of its need. From: card moved out of the sprint (work record, 2026-10-04).
- **A stream has a display name** (planned). A stream's key stays its name everywhere (the work and merge rows, the stream= fields, every verb), and gains a human label: `stream set <s> --display <name>` records one line of printable text, at most 60 bytes, on the stream's control card as its `display` field, cleared with `default` or `none` like every other stream field. The dashboard's Work table and the streams listing show the display name when set, else `point-fix-<release>` when the stream belongs to a release, else the key (sprint.StreamDisplay); the streams verb prints it beside the release, StreamClock and StreamRow carry it in `Display`, and a name over the bound or with a newline is refused whole, nothing written. From: the owner, 2026-10-11: "agree that the name becomes the key, and you add a small display name. good tidy feature. pls add.".
- **A review loop has a circuit breaker** (planned). A card is escalated to the coordinator after 4 consecutive review rounds that each bring a new blocking finding, or after 6 substantive review rounds of any kind, instead of going round again. From: the owner, 2026-10-11: a lesson from the Cockroach Labs write-up "Five months treating bugs like patients" (MOLT Sinai).
- **A red base is pushed to the coordinator** (planned). When the base a card lands onto is red, the machine pushes the coordinator a judgment naming the base and its red run. This is the push half of card a-landing-never-goes-onto-a-red-base; the landing gate itself stays in v1.3. From: the owner, 2026-10-11: a lesson from the Cockroach Labs write-up "Five months treating bugs like patients" (MOLT Sinai).
- **An acknowledged empty row is one episode while it holds** (planned). emptyConds keys the empty-row episode by its text, and the text was rebuilt from the cards waiting once the judgment no longer sat in Open, so a second ready card she could do changed the text, wrote a second NFriendEmpty judgment and closed the acknowledgement, though the conjunction (she is up, her row empty, cards she could do wait) never cleared. The episode's text now comes from the judgment the coordinator holds (an acknowledgement, or a wait not yet due) as well as from an open one, so tla/CoordinatorPass.tla's OneJudgmentAnEpisode (Kind = "empty") holds in the code: the acknowledged episode stays one until the condition clears, a card dealt to her closes it, and a later episode is judged afresh past EmptyRowAfter. From: v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11, section 9 row D9; this card.
- **A landing refuses a tla/*.cfg the case plan does not name** (planned). The lander's run-record check held the plan only to its own fields, so a head adding tla/MCFoo.cfg with no tla/CASES.tsv row, or taking a row for a configuration that stays, passed until tlacheck refused the whole plan. recordsRefusals now holds the merged tree to tlacheck's own loader, tlc.LoadCases, after ParseCases, and refuses with one line on tla/CASES.tsv; a tla/CASES.tsv edit alone holds a tree that carries models to its plan. LoadCases names, in name order, every MC*.cfg the plan does not name, every config the plan names that has no file, and every row whose module is missing, keeping its opening words. From: the seat, 2026-10-11, epoch 16; this card.
- **The page lock's comment-only check reads the page a browser renders** (planned). The stripper that proves a comment-only change renders nothing no longer mistakes four visible things for comments: an HTML text comment leaves nothing rather than a space; a comment opener inside a quoted attribute value is code; an inline script with a data-src attribute is read as JS; and a slash after a control if, while or for condition opens a regex, failing closed otherwise. The lock's header and the spec's The page lock state the comment-only form and that the card lint is ask-only. From: this card.
- **verify compares the scope its tree was imported with, not the whole organization** (planned). import --repo <org>/<name> now records the repositories it read as the work-tree's :scope, written only for a scoped import; a whole-organization tree stays byte for byte what it was, and a file without :scope reads as a whole-organization tree. verify with no --repo compares the tree's own scope (tla/WorkImport.tla's Verify already read the scope it imported), --repo narrows within it, and a --repo outside it is refused naming the scope before any GitHub call; verify --against does the same. Before, verify with no --repo read the whole organization and reported MISSING for every repository the scoped import left out. From: the card verify-defaults-to-the-trees-import-scope w2; the v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11 section 9 row D12 (code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba).
- **Every producer card has its consumer out after the tick** (planned). Adds ConsumersOut check at the end of every tick to assert that every producer card (working, fix, review) has its consumer out: an attempt held by an up member/friend for working/fix, or reads asked by up readers for review. Violations are reported as quiet judgments. Also reduces MaxSettle from 64 to 32 as per the owner's design, and changes settle bound handling to push a judgment instead of erroring the tick. From: the owner, 2026-10-11 ~10:40-11:00 AM ET, on the live epoch 17; card every-producer-card-has-its-consumer-out-after-the-tick.w1.
- **The ready-over judgment reads the deal's settled rests** (planned). A ready card whose tier is served only by a route resting at the tick's now raises the ready-over judgment (a ready card is not dealt), naming the resting route, whether the provider's recorded rest or one the rule rests this tick. The ready-over part settles the rests once as the deal does (withRests), on the snapshot the conditions are counted on, so the route the judgment names as resting is exactly one the deal does not draw; a rest whose time has ended is not named and the card is dealt. From: card ready-over-reads-the-settled-rests.w2; the seat's v1.2.14 audit, 2026-10-11.
- **The ready-over judgment is keyed on the cause, never its figures** (planned). The ready-over judgment is one per (reason, tier), keyed by the reason the deal leaves the card (condKey's NReadyOver case, readyOverWhy). The reason names figures that move while the cause stands -- a route's balance (out of budget (balance $x)) and a rest's end (resting until <stamp>) -- so as the balance moved the key changed, notify closed the old judgment and wrote a second one: one cause, a second push, and the coordinator's wait on the first lost. readyOverWhy now takes each moving figure out of the key before keying, while the What keeps it, so the judgment is rewritten in place with the latest figures and pushed once. From: the coordinator, 2026-10-11 (v1.2.14 defect ready-over-key-ignores-the-balance-amount); checked against nova-sprint main 00c54ba.
- **run refuses a negative --tick-deadline** (planned). A negative --tick-deadline is refused right after the flags are parsed, through run's usual refuse helper, before the loop starts or a server listens; the refusal names the flag, the value and that 0 waits for ever. Before, tickDeadlineOf returned 0 for any least <= 0 and tickWithin waited for ever when d <= 0, so --tick-deadline -1s switched the watchdog off with nothing said. 0 still waits for ever and every positive value behaves as today. From: nova-tools#5173 (transferred here at the split), roadmap item tick-watchdog-bounded-diagnostics, its negative-deadline half; this card.
- **The tick watchdog never waits on its own dump** (planned). An overrun's goroutine stacks are written into memory first (pprof's WriteTo into a bytes.Buffer, which cannot block), then the watchdog acts (the tick's cancel, or the wedged exit), and only then hands the buffer to stderr in a goroutine it waits on at most TickStacksBound (2 s); a stderr nobody drains (a full pipe under a supervisor, a blocked terminal) can no longer hold up the cancel or the exit, and a dump not written within the bound is dropped with one TICK STACKS line saying so. From: the card tick-watchdog-exit-never-waits-on-its-dump w2; nova-tools issue #5173, roadmap item tick-watchdog-bounded-diagnostics; code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba.
- **The stops digest counts only the stops still holding** (planned). One plan could close a stop and at the same time send an NStopsDigest saying it still holds: notify closes the open NStopMemberDown judgment of a member up again, and stopsDigest then gathered its stops from the snapshot before the plan, counting and naming the stop just closed. stopsDigest now leaves out every judgment the same plan closes, matched by note id; with no stop left it writes neither the digest nor its clock. From: v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11, section 9 row D8; card stops-digest-counts-only-held-stops.w1, id given by the coordinator 2026-10-11 (code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba).
- **init over a keyless store records the seat move, so an earlier observation lapses** (planned). init writing a coordinator name onto a store whose key holds none while a friend-health record survives (an observation made under an earlier seat) now records the move as a seat change, as the seat's own step does: the seat record and its generation stepped, written with the key, its log line and its note, so the earlier observation lapses by FriendEvidence's generation check. A fresh store's first init writes no seat record, and init over a held key keeps the holder, as before. From: this card; v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11 section 9 row D10 (code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba).
- **The lander's empty-commit refusal says a result is missing when it holds none** (planned). The lander's empty-commit check refused an empty diff with no result to read (a nil work card: the fleet row absent or the work card tidied away) with the same finding as one whose result claimed changes, "empty commit: the result claims changes the diff does not show", naming a claim nothing made. It now returns emptyCommitNoResultFinding, "empty commit: the head changes nothing from the attempt's start, and the lander holds no result to say why", and both findings return the card to review through one helper, isEmptyCommitFinding. From: this card: lander-empty-commit-says-no-result-is-held, from the v1.2.14 point-release plan and the roadmap item lander-empty-commit-handling.
- **A hook push is sent only once its record names it** (planned). When the hook record write fails, a look now delivers none of that look's pushes and undoes what it added (the note keys it marked sent, the pushes it added to the open list, and the sequence), so the next look offers them again, records them, and sends them once. The SEAT HOOK line it prints is unchanged. Before, the push was delivered while the record named no unacknowledged push, so a push delivered over a failed record write never blocked the gate: past HookAckBound a coordinator command ran though the push had been delivered and was never recorded. From: the card a-hook-push-is-sent-only-once-recorded w1; the v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11 section 9 row D7 (code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba).
- **A machine's fault down keeps another's hold mark** (planned). When presence takes a member down for a missed beat, the machine writes its own fault hold (held_by=fault, fault_since) only on a member that carries no hold: a member the sync, the adopt, its environment or the coordinator already holds keeps its hold, its mark, its reason and its finish marker when it goes down, and still goes down. Overwriting the mark hid the hold from its own release, so a held member could no longer be released and the clear left a markless hold (tla/DealFill.tla FaultHold and PersonHoldStays; docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md section 5). From: the seat's audit, 2026-10-11 (a reader finding on card a-member-environment-fault-holds-it-and-pushes-the-seatb, attempt 5, head 38c66ea7542f); this card.
- **A load over more than one read set reads the table's mark** (planned). readInto read a table of more than ntable.LimitReadSetMembers records in several read sets and checked only that each saw the table's revision, so a store that lost writes and wrote others up to the same revision between two read sets (a restart from an older save, a failover) gave one revision and two histories and the load mixed them. It now reads the mark of the change event that left the table's revision (TableChangesMarked, as markOf reads it) before the first read set and after the last, and a mark that changed is a movedError, as a changed revision is, so the load reads again under its existing retry. A table of at most 1024 records, or a backend that keeps no marks, reads as before (tla/LoadCache.tla, LoadIsSnapshot). From: the v1.2.12 inventory 2026-10-11, section 9 row D5; code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba.
- **The version verb says which fixes a build carries** (planned). nova-sprint version --features lists the fixes this build carries, one line each `<release> <fix-id> <title>`, from the fixes ledger compiled into the binary (docs/embed.go) and read with make roadmap's parser: every fix of a release at or below the build's version. A build whose version is not a release (a dev build) lists the shipped releases' fixes and says the unreleased fixes of the tree it was built from are not listed. nova-sprint version --has <fix-id> exits 0 when the build carries the fix and 1 when the ledger names it in a later release or not at all, naming which; --json prints {version, fixes:[{release,id,title}]}. From: tmp/next-sprint-cards/TOOLING-FROM-THE-SEAT-2026-10-11.md item 16 (the owner, 2026-10-11); the v1.2.10 bisect, where the coordinator ran strings on two binaries to learn whether v1.2.9 held the environment-fault fix.
- **A stats reset zeroes the unattributed spend** (planned). After nova-sprint stats reset every stream's spend counts from the mark, but the grand total did not reach zero: the cost line's <other>, the largest TierCosts.Unreconciled on any stream's record, is the sprint's UnreconciledSpend since the epoch's clear, never since the mark. ResetMark now holds the sprint's unattributed spend at the mark (in cents) and streamsSince subtracts it on every stream's record, the streams the mark does not know included, so the cost line, the dashboard's cost tile and where --json's unreconciled count from the mark, never below zero. The mark line names it beside the total. From: the seat's v1.2.14 audit, 2026-10-11 (a stats reset does not zero the grand total spent), checked against nova-sprint main 00c54ba; the owner's rule of 2026-10-09: a stats reset clears every cost figure, the total spent, per card and per tier; this card a-stats-reset-zeroes-the-unattributed-spend.
- **A stale post-STOP beat keeps its word for the settle** (planned). settleStopDebtByBeat read a machine's live set fresh-only (sprint.LiveNamesAt through liveOf), so a machine that beat once after the STOP naming its held report and then went silent past BeatDeadline had its lease settled at START: the card went back to ready at gen+1, was dealt again, and the held report was refused as stale when it came. The owner's last beat since the STOP now keeps its word fresh or stale (sprint.LiveNamedAt, no clock), as tla/StopReturn.tla SettleByBeat reads it (d.id \notin beat); tla/LiveRuns.tla's reversed witness "staleasabsent" is exactly that wrong reading: a silent row's stale beat as an empty live set. LiveNamesAt, LiveHeldAt, liveOf and LiveReturns keep their fresh-only reading. No model change. From: the coordinator 2026-10-11, added to v1.2.14 beside the v1.2.12 inventory's section 9 row D2 (a held finished report across STOP refused as stale); D2's first cause was fixed by nova-sprint #87 (15c779c); this is what that fix left; code read at nova-sprint main 00c54ba.
- **Every held_by write names a hold mark, and each mark keeps the member off the deal** (planned). Tests only, no product change. internal/sprint/hold_marks_test.go holds a table of every mark a member's held_by carries -- none (the coordinator's), the sync's, the machine's fault, the adopt's and the environment's -- each written by its own writer (a fleet hold with its HeldBy, presence's down for the fault, holdAdopting for the adopt, a finish whose report is an environment fault for envFaulted) and cleared by its own release (fleet up, the sync's release, faultClear, clearEnvFault, the adopt's finish). For each it pins the behaviour: the member is not up and dealt no card by the deal or the level, a tick presence with a fresh beat leaves held and held_by as they were, another mark's mark-scoped release leaves it held with its mark, and its own release clears it. It then scans the package's non-test .go files for every held_by assignment (a name[FieldHeldBy] = X and FieldHeldBy: X) and fails naming the value and its file:line when no table row names it, so a new hold kind cannot ship without the table checked against it. The known-yes proof is envFaulted's status line deleted: the environment row then fails at UpMembers. From: this card, card-lint-a-hold-owner-every-reader-accepts.w1, from the reader finding on a-member-environment-fault-holds-it-and-pushes-the-seatb attempt 5 (head 38c66ea7542f): the environment hold was written with held_by=environment but the member's status was left Up, so the level dealt to it and presence wrote held_by=fault over the mark.
- **A brief edit records its needs, and the deal refuses a card whose needs have not landed** (planned). A card's needs are only the column's, not the brief's: brief re-points needs only through dependsOnly (the DEPENDS-ON line the only difference), and any other edit took the ordinary path, wrote the brief and dropped the parsed needs, so on 2026-10-11 a brief --dir moved 85 briefs that now carry DEPENDS-ON while every card kept zero needs and stayed ready; and dealPlan's eligibility checked stream held, friend pin and inState(c, Ready) only, no guard on needs, so a ready card with unlanded needs was dealt. Now the ordinary brief path writes the needs the new brief's DEPENDS-ON names whenever they differ from the card's, clearing them when the brief drops its DEPENDS-ON; a ready card that gains a need not landed moves ready -> waiting in the same unit (the lifecycle accepts the move, ready -> waiting being no longer only a sentinel's effect when the edit records needs); dealPlan refuses a card with WaitsFor(s, c, nil) non-empty, and unmet judges every move to dealt (Working) against the card's stored needs, so Lawful refuses dealing a card whose needs have not landed whatever path asks for it; a card dealt or working keeps its attempt and the new needs apply from its next deal. help brief says this. Red tests in internal/sprint/needs_guard_test.go (a ready card whose brief gains an unlanded need waits with its needs recorded; a waiting or ready card whose edit names landed needs stays or becomes ready; a ready card with an unlanded need built in the store is never dealt and the tick's invariant names it; an edit with no needs change leaves them; a brief that drops its DEPENDS-ON clears the card's needs). The invariant a primary anywhere but waiting has every need landed already named such a card; this is the deal and the brief catching up (docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md, needs and the deal). From: this card, a-brief-edit-records-its-needs-and-the-deal-checks-them.w3, from the owner on the live epoch 17, 2026-10-11 ~10:40-11:00 AM ET: 89 v1212 cards ran or sat ready before their DEPENDS-ON landed (four failed four attempts each); code read at nova-sprint main 1405d26; the owner: "by definition this must not happen.".
- **The card lint refuses a header key below the prose** (planned). cardHeaderBlock ends the card header at the first prose line ("ended = true // the prose begins here") and CardHeaderValue reads only that block, so a header key written below the prose was never read and nothing said so: only the five typed keys (KIND, PATHS, TEST, LEGS, SOURCE) drew a stranded finding. A new swarm.LintHeaderStranded reuses cardHeaderBlock and returns one finding per header key (KIND, PATHS, TEST, LEGS, SOURCE, START, STOP, DEPENDS-ON, PRIORITY, NEW, SHARED, REPO, BASE, RESULT, tier) written as a KEY: line below the block, naming the key and its line; a key in the header passes and a sentence that merely mentions a key mid-line draws nothing. lintBriefReads calls it, so add, brief, recut and preflight refuse a stranded key through the same path as every other lint finding, exit 2 (preflight exit 1), nothing written. LintCardDepends (which nothing outside tests called) is deleted; its stranded-DEPENDS-ON finding is now this one, and the package doc and lineup helpers (Lineup, CardDependsRemedy, ReadLineup and their exclusive readers) that only it used are removed with it. This is the bug behind the 2026-10-11 epoch 17: 89 v1212 briefs carried DEPENDS-ON: below the REPO:/BASE: sentence, briefNeeds read no needs from any of them, add admitted every card straight to ready, and cards were dealt before their dependencies landed. From: this card: card-lint-refuses-a-header-key-below-the-prose, from the owner on epoch 17, 2026-10-11 (~10:40-11:00 AM ET); code read by the seat's reader at nova-sprint main 1405d26; the owner: "this should be caught by card lint.".
- **needs set re-points a card's needs in place** (planned). The only way to change a card's needs after admission was drop and re-add, so a card admitted with the wrong needs needed a twin. A card's needs are read once at add (briefNeeds) and a brief edit drops them on any change beyond the DEPENDS-ON line, and on 2026-10-11 ~100 frontier cards could not be re-pointed or reworked without twins. Now nova-sprint needs set <id> (--needs <a,b> | --clear) [--answers <note>] is the direct verb, the coordinator's alone: it rewrites the line the brief names its needs on (Needs: or DEPENDS-ON:, keeping that line's key; --clear takes the line off; a brief with no such line gains a DEPENDS-ON: line) so card <id> shows the truth, and it moves the card by the one lifecycle table: a ready card that gains a need not landed moves ready -> waiting, a waiting card whose new needs have all landed moves waiting -> ready, a card working or in review keeps its attempt with the new needs applying from its next deal (the brief edit's briefDepends path), and a landed or off-table card, a sentinel, and a need that is no primary on the table (named whole) are refused, exit 1, nothing written. The path is chosen by the card's column, not by whether it has ever been dealt: a card returned to waiting or ready in place after an attempt takes the lifecycle move and keeps its attempt field, so it is never sent to drop and re-add a twin. unmet now judges a move waiting -> ready by the needs the unit writes, not the ones the pre-state holds. help needs names it (docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md, needs). Red tests in cmd/nova-sprint/needs_set_test.go pin all seven: ready -> waiting with the move printed, waiting -> ready on landed needs, --clear emptying a waiting card to ready, a need not on the table refused naming it with nothing written, a dealt card keeping its attempt, a landed and a dropped card refused, and the brief's DEPENDS-ON line rewritten with no other line changed. - **A rate limit stalls its route briefly; it never fails a card or rests it for 3-in-10** (planned). A take a provider ends rate-limited (class=rate-limited) never fails the card, on any route and however many times: the card returns unspent (no FieldTakeEnded, no redeal, no attempt, no failed-work judgment, none of the out-of-credit bound FieldRateReturns) and leaves a rate_take_<n> record numbered after the last one the card holds, with no gap and no bound, so RateTakes reads every one. The route backs off briefly, then serves again by itself: RestsDue computes the backoff purely from those records, k being the route's rate-limited ends since its last ok end (a take the worker finished ok, in the finished cell or past it; a failed finish resets nothing) and last the latest one's time, ending at last + min(60s*2^(k-1), 15m) (RateBackoff) -- a fixed point in time, never relative to now. Its line is kept beside the route's own rest in the provider's rule3_rest_ property (<route>+rate-backoff), never over it, so it never moves the 3-in-10 window's mark, never blocks the coordinator's rest and is never woken; a backoff on every route of a tier makes the card wait ready, as a provider at its concurrency budget does, never a no-route judgment, and the no-stall rule holds it on the backoff whenever a route of the tier backs off and none can be drawn (never NStalled); the rebalance never moves a card onto a machine with no route it can draw; restWrites writes it and one happened note ("rate-limit backoff of <d> on <route>, until <t>") once per end, none while the same end holds, never a judgment, and drops a backoff line once its end has passed. A rate limit no longer counts toward the 3-in-10 transient rest (transient excludes classRateLimited); a 5xx window still rests the route 30 minutes, and is written over a backoff that holds. member.Judge treats a rate-limited run with no pushed head as a provider failure whatever its shape, while a shaped result that pushed a head stays the card's own. TLA+ model RateBackoff, properties RateLimitSpendsNoRedeal and BackoffBounded with the temporal BackoffEnds, reversed witnesses MCRateBackoffBrokenSpend and MCRateBackoffBrokenNoCap. Tests TestARateLimitedTakeReturnsTheCardUnspent, TestARateLimitBacksTheRouteOffBriefly, TestARateLimitedRunIsAProviderFailure, TestARateTakeIsNumberedAfterTheLastRateTake, TestARateBackoffNeverHoldsOffTheFiveHundredsRest and TestARateBackoffIsWrittenAndNotedOncePerEnd. Landed by hand after 15 sprint attempts. The no-stall rule and the rebalance test drawability with the deal's own budgets and the tier's array (backoffWait): tests TestABackedOffTierWithTheOtherProviderFullIsAWaitNeverAStall and TestABackedOffTierWithTheOtherRouteOutOfTheArrayIsAWaitNeverAStall. - **Doctor names a member whose link flapped in the last hour** (planned). On 2026-10-11 the coordinator found by hand, in b1's and b3's kernel journals, that their network links had gone down and up, and no check named it. The member probe now reads one more fact before its end marker (cmd/nova-sprint/doctor_probe.go): on Linux the kernel's link changes in DoctorLinkWindow (one hour), journalctl -k -q --no-pager --since "-1h" filtered by one extended case-insensitive grep for the drivers' link words (Link is Up, Link is Down, link up, link down, carrier lost, carrier acquired), printed as "link <count> <the last such line, cut to 160 bytes>", and on Darwin "link - not measured on darwin"; when journalctl is absent or cannot read the kernel journal (no lines and a non-zero exit, or the insufficient-permissions line) it prints "link - <why>". parseProbe reads it into MemberProbe (LinkChanges, -1 when not measured; LinkLast; LinkWhy), and DoctorMemberEnv gives a member whose link counted DoctorLinkWarnChanges or more changes in the window one WARN, never a FAIL, naming the member, the count, the last line and the remedy. doctor --preflight replaces its links WARN with the same fact as a gate: a member with that many changes is one FAIL row (area preflight, check links), so a switch or adopt is refused while a member's link flaps, and a member not measured stays a WARN. No secret is printed and the journal window is short, never the whole journal. Tests TestProbeScriptHasTheLinkFactAndQuotesNothingFromConfig and TestParseProbeReadsTheLinkFact (cmd/nova-sprint/doctor_probe_link_test.go), TestDoctorMemberEnvWarnsOnAFlappingLink and TestDoctorMemberEnvQuietOnOneOrNoLinkFact (internal/sprint/doctor_link_test.go); no test runs ssh or journalctl. docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md, the doctor's member-env check and the preflight, says the link fact and its bound. - **take by id starts a friend's card as a lane take does** (planned). The two forms of take did different things. take --as <friend> --lane <n> moved the card to working through the lane's move (laneSet), so it carried the lane and, on a friend's row, her start (friendStartSet) and the tick left it working. take --as <friend> <card>@<gen> by id moved it with friendTaken instead, which set no start, so the next tick put it back ready (friendUnstartedWorking) and her progress was refused "not working"; a lane take then re-dealt the card at a new generation and her finish was refused stale. The by-id take now goes through the lane's move too (sprint.NamedLaneTake, TakeReq.LaneByID): each named card is taken by takeOne -- so every guard a take by count holds holds for it too (the row's seat and width, the card's live generation, its route rest and the providers' fleet-wide concurrency budget) -- and is then stamped as a lane's take stamps the card it is given (laneSet: the lane when --lane <n> names one, the row's lane heard from now, and on a friend's row her start), so both forms of the verb write working, holder, lane and generation the same way. A member's by-id take is unchanged and names no lane. TAKE-BY-ID says a LANE line per card as the lane's take does. On 2026-10-11 the seat lost two takes and one finish to this. A new friendDealtOrder is the one order a friend's dealt set is filled and taken in (the ladder by a card's rank, then the stream turns over a card's stream field, then SortCards within a stream), used by the friend deal pass (friendDealPass) and by a friend's take (takeOne, through s.friendWorkRank, which reads the primary's current level so a priority change after the deal is honoured too); FriendLaneOrder is its exported face and the LANE line prints the held card's position in the deal's order. The generated ledgers docs/roadmap-evidence/fixed-<leg>.sexp are one entry per card, regenerated by the repository that owns them, the same kind the lander already merges for docs/fixes.sexp and FIXES.md, but the lander treated a conflict there as the card's own and reworked the head at the tip, a full attempt and read lost per landing (2026-10-11, about 120 schema cards). The lander now merges the evidence ledgers entry by entry (both kept, in file order, no duplicate, add/add and content conflicts alike), reads the one ledger set from cardgen.LedgerInPaths (the evidence ledgers and any path a repository's own catalog names as a ledger with a LEDGERS line in its AGENTS.md or nova.sexp, read at staging, included), and a malformed entry stops the stream with the conflict-kind ledger, never a rework.
